blocks.text: How to Score Bidders on OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030 Readiness

When every janitorial bidder checks the 'Yes, we are OSHA compliant' box on your Request for Proposal (RFP) questionnaire, a binary pass/fail checkbox tells you nothing about which vendor will actually protect your facility during a state or federal safety audit. Implementing a weighted evaluation rubric osha bloodborne pathogens clause in contracts forces contenders to prove their 29 CFR 1910.1030 compliance with verifiable documentation, realistic disinfectant dwell-time labor hours, and commercial-grade engineering controls.

Whether you manage a multi-story corporate office building where technicians service high-traffic public restrooms and wellness rooms, or a dedicated medical office building (MOB) housing outpatient clinics, your procurement scorecard should weigh regulatory verification and labor sufficiency at 55% of the total points. Below is the 100-point evaluation rubric designed for facility procurement teams.
100-Point Weighted Evaluation Rubric for OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Compliance
Grade each finalist from 0 to the maximum category points based on physical evidence submitted with their proposal package.

blocks.caption: 100-Point Proposal Scoring Matrix for OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030 Janitorial Contracts
rows: 1. Exposure Control Plan (ECP) & Training Verification
30 Points
Submits site-specific ECP updated within 12 mos, named trainer credentials, annual 1910.1030 logs, and Hep-B offer attestation.
Submits generic corporate safety handbook; promises training certificates after contract award.
Cannot produce a written ECP or mistakes general HazCom (1910.1200) for Bloodborne Pathogens (1910.1030).
2. Dwell-Time Labor Math & Specialty Rate Card
25 Points
Budgets realistic production (2,200–3,500 sq ft/hr based on clinical density), $35–$65/hr base, $55–$95/hr specialty cap, 4.33 wks/mo.
Lump-sum monthly price within $0.07–$0.15/sq ft benchmark; leaves emergency biohazard call-out rate open to T&M.
Quotes >4,800 sq ft/hr (impossible for 5–10 min disinfectant dwell times) or charges $250+ for minor restroom drops.
3. Engineering Controls & Sealed-HEPA Filtration Fleet
20 Points
Commits to sealed-HEPA commercial backpack vacuums (<=68 dBA), rigid sharps protocols, and color-coded single-zone microfiber.
Uses standard commercial vacuums without certified sealed-HEPA stages; mixes restroom and office microfiber zones.
Uses bagless residential vacuums or string mops pushed from restrooms directly into breakrooms.
4. EPA List S/B Chemistry & On-Site BBP Spill Kits
15 Points
Provides EPA reg numbers for HIV/HBV/TB disinfectants, dwell-time charts, and stages a locked BBP spill kit in every closet.
Lists general quaternary disinfectant without specifying tuberculocidal/virucidal claim or on-site solidifier kit.
Uses unverified diluted household cleaners without SDS sheets or secondary container labels.
5. COI Endorsements & Multi-Employer Indemnification
10 Points
Accepts full 1910.1030 indemnification, provides Workers' Comp Waiver of Subrogation, and carries Pollution/Pathogen endorsement.
Standard CGL ($1M/$2M) and Workers' Comp COI; requests mutual limitation of liability on OSHA fines.
Uses 1099 uninsured sub-crews or carries CGL policy with broad infectious disease/pathogen exclusion.

blocks.text: Auditing Criterion 2: Disinfectant Dwell-Time Labor vs. Square-Foot Pricing

Why does Criterion 2 tie OSHA bloodborne pathogens compliance directly to hourly production math and square-foot rates? Because EPA-registered hospital-grade and tuberculocidal disinfectants require a mandatory wet-contact dwell time—typically 3 to 10 minutes depending on the chemical formulation—to inactivate bloodborne pathogens such as Hepatitis B (HBV), Hepatitis C (HCV), and HIV-1. If a bidder quotes a rock-bottom monthly fee based on an aggressive 5,000 sq ft per hour production rate, their night cleaner only has 4 to 6 minutes total per restroom. That technician is physically forced to spray and immediately wipe dry, violating federal label instructions and rendering your bloodborne pathogens clause useless.

items.name: Step 1: Benchmark Base Per-Square-Foot Rates Against Clinical & Restroom Density
items.text: In a standard 10,000 to 24,999 sq ft corporate office ($0.07 to $0.12 per sq ft baseline at 2x/week, or 0.90x multiplier for 5x/week daily service across 21.65 visits/month), ISSA production benchmarks at 3,500 sq ft per hour. If your facility has heavy ceramic tile and grout (1.12x multiplier) or clinical exam rooms, award full points only to bids budgeting 2,200 to 2,800 sq ft per hour and pricing restroom sanitation transparently at $15 to $30 per restroom per visit.

items.name: Step 2: Verify the Specialty vs. Standard Hourly Rate Split
items.text: Confirm that routine nightly maintenance is priced at $35 to $65 per loaded labor hour (covering incidental <2 sq ft restroom blood spots and sanitary bins), while dedicated off-hours biohazard remediation or terminal decontamination dispatches are capped at $55 to $95 per hour with no more than a 2-hour minimum.

items.name: Step 3: Audit the 4.33 Weeks-Per-Month Proration Formula
items.text: Ensure the bidder calculates monthly contract value using 4.33 weeks per month (13.0 visits/month for 3x/week at a 0.95x multiplier; 21.65 visits/month for 5x/week at a 0.90x multiplier) and specifies exact per-visit deduction credits if a BBP-certified technician shift goes unstaffed.

blocks.title: Require a Live Dwell-Time Demonstration During the Vendor Interview
blocks.text: During finalist interviews, hand the vendor's operations manager the SDS and product label for their proposed restroom disinfectant and ask two simple questions: 'What is the EPA registration number on this bottle, and how many minutes must the surface remain visibly wet to kill HBV and HIV-1?' Award the full 15 points in Criterion 4 only if the operations manager answers accurately without guessing.
Scoring Criterion 3: Sealed-HEPA Filtration and Cross-Contamination Controls

In high-compliance corporate and healthcare-adjacent offices, dry particulate removal is just as important as wet disinfection. When janitorial crews use leaky upright vacuums around clinical corridors, waiting lounges, and restrooms, exhaust air aerosolizes skin squames, dried particulates, and allergen dust at breathing height. To earn all 20 points in Criterion 3, a bidder must specify commercial backpack vacuums equipped with multi-stage or sealed HEPA filtration alongside strict zone separation for mop heads and microfiber cloths.

Use three proven commercial backpack specifications as your technical benchmark when scoring a bidder's proposed equipment schedule. For large open-plan office suites and clinical corridors, the ProTeam Super Coach Pro 10 Commercial Backpack Vacuum delivers a 10-quart capacity, 4-level HEPA filtration system, an ergonomic 12.5 lb build, and low 66 dBA sound output. Where contract specifications demand a fully sealed corded unit, the Sanitaire SC412A Commercial Backpack Vacuum provides a 10-quart capacity with a sealed HEPA filtration system in an 11.5 lb frame operating at 68 dBA. For stairwells, elevator cabs, and modular clinic pods where extension cords create trip hazards during daytime or early-evening hours, the Hoover Commercial MPWR 40V Cordless Backpack Vacuum offers a 6-quart capacity, HEPA media filtration, a 14 lb ergonomic harness, and 40V brushless cordless operation.
Contract Award Thresholds and Ongoing Quarterly Audits
Once your procurement committee scores all proposals across the 100-point rubric, enforce these three governance rules before executing the contract:

items: Mandatory Minimum Score of 80/100 for High-Exposure Facilities: For medical office buildings, dental suites, urgent care centers, or corporate headquarters with on-site wellness clinics, reject any bidder scoring below 80 points overall or below 24 out of 30 points in Criterion 1 (ECP & Training Verification).

Attach the Winning Rubric Commitments as Contract Exhibit C: Incorporate the winning bidder's submitted Exposure Control Plan, EPA disinfectant registry list, sealed-HEPA equipment manifest, and $55–$95/hr specialty rate cap directly into the MSA as a binding exhibit.

Quarterly Badge-to-Certificate Cross-Audit: Every 90 days (or alongside your quarterly deep floor care schedule billed at $0.03 to $0.06 per sq ft per month), compare the building access control badge log against the vendor's current OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030 training roster to verify zero untrained replacement workers have entered the night shift.

faqs.q: Why does our evaluation rubric weight the Exposure Control Plan (30 points) higher than the monthly price (25 points)?
faqs.a: Because a single federal OSHA willful or serious citation under 29 CFR 1910.1030—or a contested workers' compensation and third-party liability claim following an unverified needlestick or improper biohazard disposal—can cost tens of thousands of dollars, wiping out any minor monthly savings from a low-ball bidder who lacks a compliant Exposure Control Plan.

faqs.q: Can a bidder use the same OSHA 1910.1200 HazCom certificate to earn points for 1910.1030 Bloodborne Pathogens training?
faqs.a: No. OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200 (Hazard Communication / GHS Safety Data Sheets) covers chemical safety, whereas 29 CFR 1910.1030 specifically covers bloodborne pathogens, OPIM handling, Hepatitis B vaccination protocols, sharps safety, and post-exposure medical evaluation. Bidders must provide separate, specific documentation for 1910.1030 to earn points in Criterion 1.

faqs.q: How do we score bidders who propose electrostatic sprayers instead of manual wiping for bloodborne pathogen compliance?
faqs.a: Award zero bonus points if electrostatic spraying is proposed as a substitute for physical soil removal. Under OSHA 1910.1030 and EPA disinfectant labels, visible blood or bodily fluid must first be physically absorbed and wiped clean using proper PPE and virucidal chemistry before any surface disinfection can achieve valid dwell-time efficacy.

faqs.q: What should we look for on the vendor's Certificate of Insurance (COI) during Criterion 5 scoring?
faqs.a: Verify active Workers' Compensation coverage matching your state's statutory limits with a Waiver of Subrogation, Commercial General Liability ($1M per occurrence / $2M aggregate minimum) naming your entity as Additional Insured, and confirmation that the policy does not exclude bodily injury or property damage arising from bacteria, viruses, or bloodborne pathogen remediation.
